summary: The main article describes a photoredox-catalyzed intramolecular aminoarylation of unactivated alkenes using aryl sulfonamides. It includes one table for reaction optimization and four figures detailing the reaction design, substrate scope, and mechanistic investigations.

items.heading: Fig. 1
items.caption: (A) Selected biologically active molecules containing arylethylamines and recent catalytic disconnections. (B) Summary of our group's prior work on aminoarylation through alkene radical cations. (C) Abstract depiction of aminoarylation cascade in the present work and challenges that were overcome.
items.description: This figure provides the context for the research, showing drug examples, previous work limitations, and the conceptual framework of the current desulfonylative aryl migration strategy.

items.heading: Fig. 2
items.caption: Structural features of the aminoarylation substrates that favor Smiles-Truce rearrangement and disfavor undesired side reactions.
items.description: This figure illustrates the design principles used to suppress dearomatization and promote the desired rearrangement by using ortho-substituents and N-acyl groups.

items.heading: Table 1
items.caption: Selected optimization trials (see ESI for complete details).
items.description: This table summarizes the screening of photocatalysts, bases, and solvents to optimize the yield of the aminoarylation product 2d.

items.heading: Fig. 3
items.caption: Scope of the aminoarylation. All reactions performed on 0.2 mmol scale. All yields are from isolation.
items.description: This figure displays the broad substrate scope of the reaction, including various aryl sulfonamides and substituted alkenes.

items.heading: Fig. 4
items.caption: (A) Newman projections depicting disfavored and favored conformers of the N-sulfonyl lactam and stereochemical outcomes of C-C bond formation. (B) Experiment establishing reactivity and catalytic turnover of deprotonated N-acylsulfonamides. (C) Mechanistic proposal of the aminoarylation. (D) Further reactions of aminoarylation products including reductive cyclization, lactam hydrolysis, and photochemical removal of an ortho substituent.
items.description: This figure details the stereochemical model, mechanistic pathway involving N-centered radicals, and synthetic applications of the resulting lactams.
